ev.q: In 2009, women were more likely than men to experience serious psychological distress during the preceding 30 days (3.6% versus 2.8%).
Percentage of Adults Aged ≥18 Years Who Experienced Serious Psychological Distress During the Preceding 30 Days
Among women, those aged 45-64 years were more likely (4.6%) to experience serious psychological distress than those aged 65-74 years (2.4%)
Among men, those aged 65-74 years (1.0%) were less likely to experience serious psychological distress than those aged 18-44 years (3.1%)
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population

methods_quotes.q: A value of 13 or more on this scale was used to define experiencing serious psychological distress.
The response values were summed to yield a scale with a 0--24 range.
